_comment: QuickBooks chart-of-accounts mapping for the monthly Stripe journal entry generated on the Revenue Recognition page. Mirrors Beau's existing entry (Aug 2026 screenshot). Edit labels here — no code change needed. `accrual_presentation`: 'append' keeps the cash lines exactly as Beau books them and ADDS the accrual (AR) adjustment lines; 'restate' replaces the 4000 cash figure with the recognized figure. `sales_tax_basis`: 'invoice' = tax on invoices billed in the month (consistent with accrual 4000); 'cash' = tax embedded in the month's deposits (Beau's historical 4050 basis). Books go-live is set in build_revenue_recognition.mjs (BOOKS_GO_LIVE) — Jan 2026 as of 2026-09-05.
_ar_writeoff_comment: NULL = no automatic write-off (Beau, 2026-09-05, final). Every invoice stays in AR until HE marks it uncollectible on the Revenue → Collections page; nothing is written off by age. The brief 90-day auto rule was removed because age alone can't tell 'gone' from 'behind' — it was writing off $8,154 from customers still paying every month (LV Service Solutions pays $699/mo with four unpaid $699 invoices). Setting a number here re-enables the age rule as a DEFAULT for undecided invoices; explicit decisions in ar_collection_overrides.json always win either way.
_revenue_split_comment: From this month revenue is recognised PER INVOICE LINE, not per charge. Allmoxy moved to multiple line items on one Stripe subscription (core software + implementation + AI tokens + custom domain), so a single charge can span several revenue accounts. Line products map to revenue types in product_revenue_types.json; types map to the accounts above. Before this month the charge-level transaction_type is used, because the line-item products did not exist yet.
